comment: The fifteen textures the castle wears, one row per name in data/scene-config.json's pixelMaterials (#742). A row is parameters and a seed; tools/pixel/index.mjs turns it into 128 x 128 RGBA and npm run pixel:render writes assets/pixel/<name>.png. test/assets.mjs re-renders every row and holds the committed PNG pixel-identical to it, so this table IS the provenance of those bytes (#743). Edit a parameter and the PNG beside it is stale until you re-render, and the suite says which row.
palettes: Every pixel is an index into the row's own `palette`, so the image can never hold more colours than the row lists; test/assets.mjs holds that at 32. Index 0 is the mortar or the gap in `courses` and `planks` (override with mortarIndex / gapIndex), and the rest is a ramp dark to light that shadeMin and shadeMax pick a band out of.
cells: Noise lattice counts, both wrapping. `courses`, `weave`: [x, y]. `planks`: [along the board, across it], which is what makes grain a grain and not a mottle. `ground`, `plaster`: [coarse, fine], square both times.

rows.name: castle_wall_slates
rows.why: 22 of the 46 wall runs. Cold grey slate in shallow courses, the castle's default stone.

rows.name: defense_wall
rows.why: The eight tower drums, under eight tints (#516), so the palette is deliberately neutral warm grey: a tint multiplies it and a coloured stone would fight the tint.

rows.name: grassy_cobblestone
rows.why: The outer ward underfoot. Setts sunk in turf: grass in the base ramp, stone in the stones.

rows.name: stone_pavers
rows.why: The base ground, the whole inner ward. Big dressed slabs, wide joints, pale enough to read at a grazing angle.

rows.name: wooden_gate
rows.why: Four gate leaves. Vertical boards, long, nearly no joints, dark oak against the pale jamb.

rows.name: rock_tile_floor
rows.why: The chapel's bay and two room floors. Large cool tiles, tight joints, the least busy of the seven course rows.

rows.name: floor_tiles_02
rows.why: One room floor. Small buff tiles, near square at 16 px, so a room wearing it reads finer than one wearing the pavers.

rows.name: old_planks_02
rows.why: Two wall runs and five room floors. Weathered grey-brown, the widest grain of the four plank rows and the most joints.

rows.name: wood_planks
rows.why: Ten room floors and the wall walk's decking, the most-used floor in the castle. Mid brown, long boards, few joints.

rows.name: dirty_carpet
rows.why: One room floor. A basket weave at 8 px, dull madder, the one soft surface in the castle and the only row in its family.

rows.name: medieval_blocks_02
rows.why: Thirteen wall runs, the second stone of the castle. Tan, warmer and larger-coursed than the slate, so a room in it reads as a different room.

rows.name: castle_brick_02_red
rows.why: Brick, and the one row whose index 0 is LIGHTER than its blocks: pale lime mortar between red bricks at an 8 px course, which is the finest course in the table.

rows.name: plastered_wall_04
rows.why: Eight wall runs, the interior partitions. No feature to line up at all, which is the point: the palette is what tells it from the stone next to it.

rows.name: wood_floor_deck
rows.why: Eight room floors. Narrow boards at 8 px against wood_planks's 16, which is the whole difference between a tower chamber's floor and a hall's.

rows.name: forest_ground_06
rows.why: The ground west of the barbican (#541), seen from the walk and two tower roofs and never stood on. Dark earth with leaf litter in the stone slot.
